idiom_name: when-expression over a sealed message hierarchy plus a Map<RouteKey, SendChannel<Message>>; select { onReceive } to merge several inbound channels
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines channels replace the router class: keep one SendChannel (or a Flow per route) for every destination and one ReceiveChannel for the input, then dispatch each element with an exhaustive when over the sealed message hierarchy so an unrouted subtype is a compile error. select { onReceive } merges several inbound channels when the router itself has multiple inputs, and because channel send suspends, a slow route applies backpressure through the router instead of dropping messages - a semantics the classic fire-and-forget router never had. Keep the rule table as a separate value (or load it from configuration) when routes must change; otherwise the when-expression plus a route map is both the idiomatic and the more testable form, since the routing function can be a pure function under test.
pitfalls: Channels created outside a CoroutineScope leak when the router stops: tie every route channel to a scope and close it on shutdown, or consumers await forever.
A rendezvous or full buffered channel suspends the sender, so one stalled destination backpressures the whole router - size buffers per route or give each route its own dispatcher.
select is biased toward the first clause, so fairness between multiple inbound channels needs explicit handling (a common surprise under load).
A when used as a statement without an else silently ignores a new message subtype; only the expression form with an exhaustive sealed hierarchy protects routing.
